title: Introduce versioned telemetry enrichment proxy and client capability handshake
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Problem: Console creates multi-source telemetry (SDK, CLI, server) with divergent field shapes and enrichment needs. We need a path to evolve analytics schemas and enrichment logic without breaking consumers or requiring coordinated deploys across many SDK/CLI versions.

Proposal: Implement a versioned telemetry enrichment proxy (VTEP) that sits in the ingest path for console telemetry. VTEP will: 1) validate incoming events against a declared schema version, 2) perform stable enrichment (user metadata, cost buckets, sampling tags), 3) expose a capability-handshake endpoint so SDK/CLI can declare supported schema ranges, and 4) emit a normalized canonical envelope tagged with the resolved schema version. The proxy will support runtime transforms (forward/backward compatibility adapters) to enable zero-downtime schema rollouts and graceful client negotiations.
acceptance_criteria: VTEP deployed to staging behind telemetry gateway and receiving test events
SDK handshake path defined: clients can POST /handshake with capability vector and receive accepted schema range and recommended client actions
VTEP performs validation and rejects clearly malformed payloads with helpful error codes for clients
Support runtime mapping rules for minor-version additions (non-breaking) and fallback transforms for removed/renamed fields
A rollout plan for gradual adoption (canary routes, percentage rollouts) documented and runnable via console rollouts UI
End-to-end test demonstrating older SDK (simulated) sending v1.2 events being normalized to v2.0 canonical envelope and landing in analytics datastore
tasks: Design handshake API and capability vector format
Implement validation layer using JSON Schema + semantic version matcher
Build enrichment adapters (user lookup, cost bucketing, region tags)
Implement transform engine with safety rules and feature gates
Add observability: per-schema metrics, reject rates, handshake mismatch dashboards
SDK/CLI changes: add optional handshake call and graceful fallback paths (implementation stubs in SDK repo)
Run canary rollout and verify queries/dashboards are stable
notes: Decision: Use semantic versioning (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH) for schemas. Backwards-incompatible changes require MAJOR bump and rollout policy; MINOR allows additive fields with transforms; PATCH is for documentation/metadata only.

Trade-off: Doing transforms in the ingest path increases CPU cost but simplifies downstream analytics and avoids costly retroactive ETL. We'll introduce a configurable CPU budget per VTEP instance and prefer idempotent, stateless transforms.
Edge case: SDKs that are air-gapped may never handshake. Default behavior: accept legacy payloads using compatibility adapters and emit a 'legacy_client' tag for downstream filtering.
Security: handshake endpoint will be rate-limited and authenticated by existing telemetry write tokens. Audit logging required for transforms that drop or rewrite PII fields.
Privacy: PII redaction transforms must be whitelisted in release notes and audited by Security before enabling in production.
